key_insight: A compact Rosenhead-profile trefoil vortex in a large periodic box can evolve into decaying turbulence with a Kolmogorov-like energy spectrum and structure-function scaling.
engineering_relevance: This suggests unforced Navier–Stokes simulations may be useful as controlled turbulence generators for benchmarking experiments and testing high-Reynolds-number flow physics.
method: Extend a compact trefoil vortex simulation to later times in a (4π)^3 periodic domain.
Use an algebraic Rosenhead vorticity profile to improve compactness and reduce boundary influence.
Analyze energy spectra, structure functions, and vorticity moments during decay and pre-reconnection evolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports persistent Kolmogorov scaling, structure-function scaling, finite-energy dissipation independent of viscosity, and power laws E(t)~(t+t0)^-10/7 and ℓ(t)~(t+t0)^(2/7).
watch_item: Reported scaling is sensitive to whether the lowest Fourier modes of the periodic domain are included, so finite-box effects must be handled carefully.
paper_title: Generating Kolmogorov spectra and structure functions with a Rosenhead profile trefoil vortex knot
